name: High Power Electric Device
description: A self-propelled vehicle, other than a motor vehicle that must be titled and registered, whose electric motor can carry it past 20 mph on motor power alone, including any e-bike tampered with beyond its factory speed or power settings or modified to exceed 20 mph on the motor.

restrictions.rule: Powered by an electric motor capable of more than 20 mph on motor power alone
An e-bike with equipment modified or tampered with beyond the manufacturer's settings to change its speed or power output, or made to exceed 20 mph on motor power alone, becomes one
Ridden under every traffic-code rule that applies to a motorcycle operator
Riders under 16 may not ride one on a highway, and the owner may not let them
Riders 16 and older may ride one on a highway with a class D driver license and no motorcycle endorsement
restrictions.citation: Utah Code §53-3-202, as amended by H.B. 381 (2026)

restrictions.rule: Riders under 21 must wear a helmet on a highway, an infraction fined up to $110 rather than an e-bike's $25
The Driver License Division says it must be street-legal (lights, mirrors and other equipment) and registered with the Division of Motor Vehicles to ride on public roads
One without a VIN that isn't a motorcycle doesn't need liability insurance
Local authorities and state agencies may regulate or ban it on sidewalks, paths and trails they control
Commercial sellers must tell buyers the state's insurance and registration requirements

Sellers must disclose at sale and in any advertising, website or social media post, in bold capitals at least the size of its description, that it is not an electric assisted bicycle but a motor vehicle subject to motor vehicle laws, and that insurance may not cover it

Commercial sellers must disclose at sale and in any advertising, website or social media post, in bold capitals, that it is not an electric assisted bicycle but a motor vehicle subject to motor vehicle laws, that a helmet may be required, and that insurance may not cover it
restrictions.citation: Utah Code §§41-6a-1115.5(8), 41-6a-1511(6), as amended and enacted by H.B. 381 (2026)

restrictions.rule: A peace officer who sees a rider under 18 commit a violation may hold it and release it only to a parent or guardian
